cases.topics: P waves; S waves; seismic evidence
facts: P waves can travel through solids and fluids.
S waves travel through solids but not through fluids.
Changes in seismic-wave speed and direction provide evidence about boundaries inside Earth.
A seismic shadow zone is a region where particular direct seismic waves are not recorded.
cases.summary: Seismic waves reveal Earth structure. Seismic waves reveal Earth structure.

keyTerms.definition: An S wave is a shear wave that does not travel through fluids.
keyTerms.example: The absence of direct S waves across part of Earth supports the inference of a liquid outer core.

facts: An operational definition states how a concept will be measured or observed.
Reliability concerns whether a measurement produces consistent results.
Validity concerns whether a measurement captures the concept it is intended to represent.
An observed association alone does not establish a causal relationship.
cases.summary: Operationalization connects concepts to observations. Operationalization connects concepts to observations.

keyTerms.definition: An operational definition specifies the observable procedure used to represent a concept.
keyTerms.example: A study defines civic participation by the activities counted and the time window measured.

facts: The generic size of a written interval counts letter names inclusively.
Specific interval quality depends on both generic size and semitone distance.
The generic sizes of inversion pairs sum to nine.
Under inversion, major pairs with minor while perfect remains perfect.
